title: A finite module over a Noetherian ring has a resolution by finite free modules (Stacks 00LP)
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $M$ a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Then there exist integers $n_0,n_1,n_2,\ldots\ge0$ and $R$-linear maps forming an exact complex $$\cdots\to R^{\oplus n_2}\xrightarrow{d_2}R^{\oplus n_1}\xrightarrow{d_1}R^{\oplus n_0}\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}M\to0,$$ i.e. $\varepsilon$ is surjective, $\ker\varepsilon=\operatorname{im}d_1$ and $\ker d_i=\operatorname{im}d_{i+1}$ for all $i\ge1$; in particular it is a resolution of $M$ by finite free $R$-modules.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00LP (lemma-resolution-by-finite-free, line 17411), part (2), with its proof (lines 17428--17436). Tag verified in tags/tags: 00LP,algebra-lemma-resolution-by-finite-free

proof.text: Base step. Since $M$ is finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], choose generators $m_1,\ldots,m_{n_0}\in M$ and let $\varepsilon:R^{\oplus n_0}\to M$ be the $R$-linear map sending the $j$-th standard basis vector $e_j$ to $m_j$. Every element of $M$ is an $R$-linear combination $\sum_j a_jm_j=\varepsilon(\sum_j a_je_j)$, so $\varepsilon$ is surjective. (Put $F_{-1}=M$, $d_0=\varepsilon$.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00LP (lemma-resolution-by-finite-free), proof of part (2), lines 17428--17436 ('As a first step choose a surjection $R^{n_0}\to M$')

proof.text: Inductive step. Suppose for some $e\ge0$ an $R$-linear map $d_e:R^{\oplus n_e}\to F_{e-1}$ has been constructed (with $F_{e-1}=R^{\oplus n_{e-1}}$ for $e\ge1$ and $F_{-1}=M$). Let $K_e=\ker d_e\subseteq R^{\oplus n_e}$. The module $R^{\oplus n_e}$ is finitely generated (by $e_1,\ldots,e_{n_e}$) [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], so its submodule $K_e$ is finitely generated [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite]. As in the base step choose generators $k_1,\ldots,k_{n_{e+1}}$ of $K_e$ and let $d_{e+1}:R^{\oplus n_{e+1}}\to R^{\oplus n_e}$ send $e_j\mapsto k_j$; then $\operatorname{im}d_{e+1}=K_e=\ker d_e$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00LP (lemma-resolution-by-finite-free), proof of part (2), lines 17428--17436 ('choose a surjection $R^{n_{e+1}}\to\Ker(R^{n_e}\to R^{n_{e-1}})$ which is possible because $R$ is Noetherian'); the finiteness of the kernel is Algebra, Lemma 00IK (lemma-Noetherian-basic), second assertion

proof.text: Iteration. Applying the inductive step for $e=0,1,2,\ldots$ (definition by recursion on $e$, choosing at each stage generators of $K_e$) gives integers $n_0,n_1,n_2,\ldots\ge0$ and maps $\varepsilon=d_0$, $d_1,d_2,\ldots$ with $\operatorname{im}d_{e+1}=\ker d_e$ for every $e\ge0$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00LP (lemma-resolution-by-finite-free), proof of part (2), lines 17428--17436 ('having constructed an exact complex of length $e$ we simply choose ...')

proof.text: Exactness. By the base step $\varepsilon$ is surjective, i.e. the sequence is exact at $M$; by the iteration $\operatorname{im}d_1=\ker\varepsilon$ and $\operatorname{im}d_{i+1}=\ker d_i$ for all $i\ge1$. In particular $d_i\circ d_{i+1}=0$ and $\varepsilon\circ d_1=0$, so $\cdots\to R^{\oplus n_1}\to R^{\oplus n_0}\to M\to0$ is an exact complex of finite free $R$-modules, as claimed.
